# Beebeeb Desktop 0.8.22 - Windows: a long download no longer fails after 60 seconds, and you can see its progress

0.8.22 fixes the most visible download problem in 0.8.21 on Windows. Windows ends a download that shows it no progress for 60 seconds and asks for the file again from the start. 0.8.21 reported nothing until the whole file had arrived, so a large cloud-only file could be downloaded twice, and opening it could fail. 0.8.22 reports a download's progress to Windows while it runs, and shows it in the tray and in Activity. This release is for Windows and Linux; macOS follows in a later version.

**What this release does not do yet:** a cloud-only file still opens only once the whole file has downloaded, as in 0.8.21. The code that lets a program read a file while it downloads is in this build, but it is switched off: in our tests, a buffered `robocopy` of a file being read while it downloads failed, so streaming stays off. It is planned for 0.8.23.

**Known limitations:**
- **Windows, opening a large cloud-only file:** the program you open it with waits until the whole file has downloaded. In our test, against local test servers with the app's 12,500 KB/s download limit, opening a 1.07 GiB file returned after 91.4 seconds.
- **Windows, the speed shown while a file downloads:** with the app's own download limit set (Settings › Sync › Download rate limit) and a connection faster than that limit, the speed in the tray and in Activity jumps between bursts and pauses. In our test (1.07 GiB, the limit at 12,500 KB/s, local test servers) it read 0.03–222.5 MB/s against an average of 12.4 MB/s, and showed no speed in 32 of 84 readings. The download itself keeps to the limit; the percentage moves in the same jumps.
- **Windows, the progress row after a download:** the row stays at 100% until the app has handed the whole file to Windows. In our tests it disappeared about 4 seconds (300 MB) and 17 seconds (1.07 GiB) after the program that opened the file had read all of it.
- **Windows, a cancelled download:** if Windows cancels a download (for example when you cancel a copy), the tray says the file couldn't finish downloading, for up to 15 minutes.
- **Windows, `robocopy` of a cloud-only file:** without `/J`, robocopy reads the file in 1 MiB pieces, and for each piece the app downloads the whole file again. In our test, 3.5 minutes of such a copy downloaded 8.57 GB to copy 25 MiB of a 344 MB file. It is the same in 0.8.21 (task LD-0110). Until it's fixed, use `robocopy /J`, copy in Explorer, or first make the file available on this device (right-click → Always keep on this device).
- **Windows, memory:** while a cloud-only file downloads, the app holds the whole file in memory: +1,556 MiB (about 1.5 GiB) for a 1.07 GiB file in our test. As in 0.8.21 (task LD-0110).
- **Windows, closing the program doesn't stop the download:** if you close the program that opened a cloud-only file, the download still runs to the end. In our test, 9 of the download's 21 requests started after the program was closed. As in 0.8.21 (task LD-0110).
- **Windows, "Free up space" on a file that is only partly on this PC, or not on it at all,** downloads the whole file first, then frees it. The end result is right; it takes the time of a download. As in 0.8.21 (task LD-0107).
- **Windows, a file fetched in parts:** Windows can fetch a cloud-only file in several parts, for example when `robocopy` copies it without `/J`. If the file is replaced on another device between two parts, the copy on this PC can hold parts of both versions. As in 0.8.21 (task 2180). This build contains a fix, but only the switched-off streaming code uses it; a whole-file download, the only kind in this release, does not.
- **Still as in 0.8.21:**
  - The files of the same name that 0.8.18 made (the 89 on the maintainer's PC) are still in Beebeeb. Deleting, renaming or saving one of them on the PC can act on the wrong copy. A delete moves that copy to the trash, where you can restore it. Sorting them out is a separate step, reviewed by hand first.
  - "Free up space" does not work on a read-only file yet. Backing up Documents, Desktop and Pictures copies a read-only file once, but does not update that copy when the original changes.
  - **Linux:** the Linux app cannot sign in yet. It has no support for a system password store, and it does not keep a sign-in any other way, so its sign-in window says "This feature is not available on this device."
  - **Shared folders:** the code is in this build; whether you see them depends on a switch on our servers, which was off at our last check (2026-11-05).

### What's New

- **[Windows] A long download no longer fails after 60 seconds (LD-0105).**
  - **Before:** the app told Windows nothing until the whole file had downloaded and been decrypted. Windows ended a download that showed no progress for 60 seconds and started it again. On the maintainer's PC with 0.8.21, a 349 MB video was downloaded twice, and one open of a 1.05 GiB file failed after 120.9 seconds (`0x800701AA`).
  - **Now:** while data arrives, the app reports the download's progress to Windows about every 5 seconds. If no data arrives for 30 seconds, it stops reporting, so a dead connection still ends the open within about 90 seconds of the last data instead of hanging.
  - **Tests:** 9 tests that run on every platform. One of them, a storage download whose chunk takes 66 seconds, failed on 0.8.21's code (1 progress report, 65 seconds without one) and passes now (473 reports, never more than 1.3 seconds without one). A native Windows test keeps a fetch open for 90 seconds: Windows sends 1 fetch with the reports, and 2 (its timer fired) with them removed.
  - **On native Windows,** against local test servers with the app's 12,500 KB/s download limit, a cloud-only 1.07 GiB video opened in 1 fetch: 18 storage requests, 0 repeated, 0 timeouts, open after 91.4 seconds, and the file was byte-identical to the one uploaded.
- **[Windows] You can see a download's progress (LD-0105).**
  - While a cloud-only file downloads, the tray's Recent list shows it as "Downloading" with the percentage, the speed and a bar, and Activity › Timeline lists it in an "In progress" card ("Files arriving on this PC."). When no data arrived recently, the row shows no speed rather than "0 B/s".
  - When a download fails, its row says "Couldn't finish downloading" and stays for 15 minutes, and the tray header says "1 file couldn't finish downloading" instead of showing everything as synced.
  - Uploads are not shown in these download rows or in the card.
  - **Tests:** 16 new Rust tests (18 of 18 deliberate breakages caught) and 6 new frontend tests. On native Windows, before the change (`e93800c`), 0 of 29 one-second readings of the tray's data had a row during a 300 MB download, and an upload showed in the "In progress" card as an unnamed row reading "Downloading". With the change, during the 1.07 GiB open above, 95 of 96 readings showed the file's row, named, its progress never going backwards (the other one was taken before the fetch arrived). An upload's row reached the download surfaces 0 times.
- **[Windows, Linux] Built on beebeeb-core v0.2.0** (https://github.com/beebeeb-io/core/releases/tag/v0.2.0). 0.8.21 was built on a core commit from 3 November. v0.2.0 adds 17 commits to it (12 of them not merges): the range-read code that streaming uses (switched off in this build), a module split and dependency updates.

### Bug Fixes / Hardening

- **[Windows] A start never removes Beebeeb's Explorer registration.** As in 0.8.20, 0.8.21 removed it and registered again when it could not read the registration's version or found an older one. In a test on a test folder, removing a registration removed 3 of its 5 placeholders from the PC (the cloud-only and partly downloaded ones) and turned the other 2 into plain files. Now an existing registration is always kept. A native Windows test starts twice on a fresh registration and keeps 5 of 5 placeholders. No test drives the unreadable or older version; the code keeps the registration in those cases too.
- **[Developer] The sync folder is registered for progressive reading,** which 0.8.23's streaming needs (it was "partial", which Microsoft documents as not currently supported). Nothing changes for you now. On the test PC, an upgrade from 0.8.21's registration with the release code kept 11 of 11 test files in their state, and a native Windows test that upgrades a folder with 5 placeholders (cloud-only, partly and fully downloaded, pinned and not) keeps all 5 unchanged.

### Verification

- Release code: `release/0.8.22`, cut at `c24a3a364dcce09e4fee9ecc4f5c47527208b25b` on `main` (the merge of desktop PR #227, which follows #225 at `e93800c`), plus the merge of the pull request that adds these notes. The notes change no app code, so the counts below are those of `c24a3a3`.
- Continuous integration at `981a107` (Desktop CI run 42191760465, PR #227's last run), whose source tree is identical to `c24a3a3`'s (tree `a1e814d`): 8 of 8 checks passed.
  - Linux, `cargo test --locked`: the library reported `test result: ok. 2393 passed; 0 failed; 7 ignored`, and three integration suites ran 33, 10 and 3 tests, all with 0 failed. 2,439 of 2,439 tests passed.
  - Windows (GitHub's Windows runner), `cargo test`: the library reported `test result: ok. 2234 passed; 0 failed; 7 ignored`, and the same three suites ran 33, 10 and 3, all with 0 failed. 2,280 of 2,280 tests passed.
  - macOS (not in this release), `cargo test`: the library reported `test result: ok. 2739 passed; 0 failed; 9 ignored`, and the three suites 33, 10 and 3. 2,785 of 2,785 tests passed.
  - Frontend: `bun test` 2157 pass / 0 fail across 119 files; the same job's `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` steps passed.
  - The run on `main` at `c24a3a3` (42194936105) passed 7 of 8 checks with the same counts on Linux, macOS and the frontend. On Windows the library reported 2233 passed, 1 failed: `ld0105_f2b_native_a_buffered_robocopy_copies_a_file_served_in_session_pieces`, a test of the streaming code that is off in this build, where 1 of 3 `robocopy` runs ended with ERROR 379. The same test passed on the same tree in the run above.
- Native Windows 11, on the maintainer's PC, the release-candidate rung at `c24a3a3`, on a separate test sync folder registered under its own test provider id, against local test servers (the person's own sync folder, Explorer registration and vault untouched; the test process talked only to 127.0.0.1):
  - The build: `cargo test --locked --lib --no-run` of `c24a3a3` with a test harness module added (never committed) and the app crate's debug assertions off, so streaming is off exactly as in a release build. The process logged `W2_STREAMING=false` and read the folder's policy back as progressive.
  - (1) Opening a cloud-only 1.07 GiB video: 1 fetch, 18 storage requests, 0 repeated, 0 timeouts, open after 91.4 seconds, SHA-256 identical to the uploaded file.
  - (2) The registration read-back on an upgrade: a folder registered with 0.8.21's policy read back "partial"; started again with the release code, it read back progressive, and 11 of 11 files kept their state.
  - (3) The progress row: 95 of 96 one-second readings of the tray's data during that open showed one row named `big-v.mp4`, direction download, progress from 0 to the file's size and never backwards (the other reading was taken before the fetch arrived); 18 of 18 five-second readings showed it too; once the app had handed the file to Windows, 0 rows.
  - (4) "Discard and download again" on a file that is not in the needs-attention state answers `not_poisoned`.
- Core: 0.8.21 pinned `d3b40e336acbbbbe34e0e793c840834fdb7f683b`; 0.8.22 pins `3db0cc26f2866564f786ffa9cb0c403d2dad0e9c`, the commit tag `v0.2.0` points to (`Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock`). `git rev-list --count d3b40e3..3db0cc2` in core: 17.
- Release workflow check: `node scripts/release-channel-checks.mjs notes 0.8.22 alpha --no-macos`, the form the release workflow uses while `[macOS]` items bind, passes on these notes; without `--no-macos` it fails, as it should.
- Real hardware smoke test: the release-candidate rung above ran on the maintainer's PC from a test build of the release code, not from the signed installer. After the alpha publish, the signed 0.8.22 alpha was installed on the maintainer's Windows 11 PC, and the maintainer reported that it works (2026-11-06, before the stable promotion).
- Not verified:
  - the signed installer on real hardware before the alpha publish (it was installed and used after it, see above);
  - a failed download's row on native Windows (covered by the Rust tests only);
  - Linux on real hardware;
  - downloads from this build against production storage (the tests ran against local test servers);
  - macOS: not in this release.

### Install / Update

This release is published to the alpha channel first. Windows installs following that channel receive it through the in-app updater; stable installs receive it only once it is promoted to stable.

macOS: not in this release; it follows in a later version.

For a fresh Windows install, download the NSIS `setup.exe` from the GitHub release assets.
